title: V5: a superseded execute child does not block a goal from closing
spec:
Evidence (luna-inbox 2026-10-07): planner_runs.decision_points (orchestrator/planner_runs.py ~328) yields closable only
when every execute child has merged_into. A superseded execute child (luna T-0603, a no-code re-gate round whose target merged
another way) blocked goal T-0593 from closing for about 10 h until the Planner set merged_into on it by hand.
Fix: exclude children with status superseded from that all(merged_into) check, and require at least one non-superseded
execute child. failed still blocks, so a real failure reaches the Planner.
Tests (tests/test_planner_runs.py): test_superseded_child_does_not_block_closable, test_failed_child_still_blocks_closable.
Run: PYTHONPATH=tests uv run python -m unittest tests.test_planner_runs. Commit on the task branch.

result.summary:
A goal can now close when one of its execute children is superseded. The closable check in `decision_points` skips superseded children and needs at least one other execute child, all of them merged. A failed child still blocks closing, so real failures still reach the Planner.

Both new tests and the full `tests.test_planner_runs` suite pass (89 tests). This is committed on `task/T-1711`. The full gate (`tests-green.sh`) is left to the daemon.

**Files changed:**
- `orchestrator/planner_runs.py`: the change to the closable check, plus an updated docstring.
- `tests/test_planner_runs.py`: added `test_superseded_child_does_not_block_closable` and `test_failed_child_still_blocks_closable`.

**Failures-only test output:** none.
